scope: Six complete bilingual units newly read: revised57b29, neighbors57b28/b30, and50b178–180. A separate English-only flow reread covers57b28–30 only. No repeated five-chapter full read is claimed.
flowJudgement: The questions flow into the Bao-qin tease, Bao-yu's correction and emotional excess, then Nightingale's calming explanation. The two replacements preserve voice, pacing and knowledge boundaries.

English.text: Xiang-yun’s illness had now passed, and she came to see him every day. Once he had his wits about him, she acted out his wild behaviour for him, making him bury his face in the pillow and laugh. He had known nothing of what he was doing at first, and even now scarcely believed it when people told him.
When they were alone, with Nightingale beside him, Bao-yu took her hand again.
‘Why did you frighten me?’
‘I was only teasing you, and you took it seriously.’
‘But what you said was so reasonable and convincing. How could it have been a joke?’

‘I made it all up,’ she said, smiling. ‘There really is no one left in the Lin family, except perhaps some very distant relations. None of the clan lives in Suzhou now. They’re scattered about the provinces, with no settled home. Even if someone did come for her, Her Old Ladyship would never let her go.’
‘Even if Grandmother would, I wouldn’t.’

‘Would you really refuse?’ Nightingale asked with a smile. ‘Perhaps it’s only talk. You’re growing up now. You’re even engaged. In another two or three years, when you’ve married, who else will you have eyes for?’
Bao-yu was startled again.
‘Who’s engaged?

contexts.assessment: Nightingale retracts the invented Lin-family story before testing Bao-yu with a supposed engagement. His earlier loss of awareness and Xiang-yun's imitation remain distinct from later conscious behaviour. The source-spanning question continues into b29.

English.text: ‘Engaged to whom?’
‘Before the New Year I heard Her Old Ladyship say she wanted to settle a match with Miss Bao-qin,’ Nightingale said with a smile. ‘Why else would she be so fond of her?’

‘Everyone calls me a fool, but you’re a bigger fool than I am,’ Bao-yu said with a laugh. ‘It was only a joke. She’s already promised to Academician Mei’s family. If I really were engaged to her, would you find me like this? When I swore those oaths and tried to smash this wretched thing before, didn’t you try to stop me and say I was mad? I’ve only just got better, and you start provoking me again.’
He ground his teeth as he spoke.

‘I wish I could die this very instant and burst my heart open for you all to see. Then let all of me, skin and bones, turn to ash. No, ash still leaves a trace. Better to turn into smoke. But smoke can gather and still be seen. It would have to be scattered in every direction at once by a great wild wind. Only then would it be right!’
Tears rolled down his face again.

contexts.assessment: PASS. Before the New Year restores the backward reference without asserting a festival date or narratorial proof of the tease. Academician Mei now matches the earlier accepted description. Her real existing engagement is distinguished from the proposed Bao-yu match. Attempted jade-smashing, teeth grinding and the ash–smoke–wind emotional escalation remain complete and unchanged.

English.text: Nightingale hastened to cover his mouth and wipe his tears away. Then she hurriedly smiled and explained.
‘Don’t upset yourself. I was worried, and that’s why I tested you.’
Bao-yu was more bewildered than ever.
‘What were you worried about?’
‘You know I don’t belong to the Lin family,’ she said, smiling. ‘I was one of the maids here, like Aroma and Faithful, only I happened to be given to Miss Lin.

contexts.assessment: Nightingale's mouth-covering and tear-wiping lead to her stated motive for testing him and her Jia-household origin. The revised time phrase has not changed who knows what or shifted the question to a narrator-certified engagement.

English.text: Grandmother Jia returned to the subject of Bao-qin gathering plum blossom in the snow, saying that the sight had been lovelier than a painting. She went on to ask in detail about the eight characters of Bao-qin’s birth date and time, and about her family’s circumstances. Aunt Xue guessed that she was probably thinking of a match for Bao-yu. She herself would have welcomed it, but Bao-qin was already promised to the Mei family. As Grandmother Jia had said nothing openly, Aunt Xue could not take it upon herself to assume anything. She therefore told her, partly revealing and partly withholding:

‘It’s a pity the child has had so little good fortune. Her father died the year before last. She’s seen a great deal of the world since she was small, though. She went everywhere with her parents, all over the mountains. Her father loved enjoying himself. He had business in different places and took his family along, spending a year travelling about one province, then half the next year in another. They must have covered five or six tenths of the whole country. The year they were here, he promised her to Academician Mei’s son. Then, the very next year, he died, and her mother has a phlegm disorder.’
Xi-feng did not wait for her to finish, but sighed and stamped her foot.
‘What bad luck! I was just going to make a match for her, and now she’s promised to someone already.’
‘Who were you going to match her with?’ Grandmother Jia asked, smiling.
‘Never you mind, old ancestor. I’d made up my mind those two were meant for one another.

contexts.assessment: Aunt Xue infers Grandmother's intention; Grandmother has not spoken openly. The Mei engagement predates this conversation. Academician Mei is already the project's wording here.

English.text: ‘But now she’s promised, there’s no point saying anything. Better leave it unsaid.’

Grandmother Jia understood what Xi-feng meant. Hearing that Bao-qin was already engaged, she too let the subject drop. They chatted for a while longer, then dispersed. The night passed without anything to relate.

contexts.assessment: Grandmother understands the implication and drops the idea on hearing that Bao-qin is already engaged. No settled new engagement is announced.

English.text: Next day the snow had cleared. After the meal, Grandmother Jia again instructed Xi-chun herself.

‘Cold or warm, go on painting. If it really can’t be ready by the New Year, so be it. The most important thing is to put in Qin as she was yesterday, with the maid and the plum blossom, exactly as they looked. Not a brushstroke wrong. Add them as soon as you can.’
Xi-chun found this difficult, but could only agree. Presently everyone came to watch her paint. She simply sat lost in thought.

‘Let her think it out by herself,’ Li Wan said to the others with a smile. ‘We can talk. Grandmother said yesterday we were to make lantern riddles. When we got home, Qi and Wen and I couldn’t sleep, so I made up two with answers from the Four Books. They each made up two as well.’
